description:
Physics and collision queries in the running world: traces, overlaps, simulation state, pushes and ragdolls.
Workflow: get_collision_channels (which channel names exist) -> line_trace / overlap_test to probe the world ->
get_physics to inspect a body -> set_simulate (undo puts the object back) -> add_impulse to push it (not undoable) ->
ragdoll for skeletal meshes.
name: physics

tools.description:
Pushes a simulating object. Not undoable (the motion that follows cannot be reverted).
Returns: The pushed actor and its velocity right after the push. Fails if the target is not simulating physics (call set_simulate first).
This cannot be undone: only call it after explicit direction or permission from the user.

at.description: Apply at this world point [x,y,z] (adds spin); default the centre of mass. ([x, y, z] (cm))

impulse.description: [x,y,z]; a velocity change in cm/s with velocity_change, else an impulse in kg*cm/s, e.g. [0,0,500]. ([x, y, z] (cm))

target.description: Simulating actor or "actor#Component", e.g. "n12". (Reference to PrimitiveComponent: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path)

velocity_change.description: Treat impulse as a velocity change (ignores mass).

tools.name: physics.add_impulse

returnValue.description: The pushed actor and its velocity right after the push. Fails if the target is not simulating physics (call set_simulate first).
returnValue.title: PhysicsToolImpulseResult

tools.description:
Lists the collision channels (trace channels and object types) and collision profiles of this project, for use with line_trace / overlap_test `channel` (Epic scene.get_collision_channels).
Returns: {channels:[{name, trace, object_type}] in engine order, profiles:[names] sorted}.
tools.name: physics.get_collision_channels

returnValue.description: {channels:[{name, trace, object_type}] in engine order, profiles:[names] sorted}.

channels.description: Trace channels and object types, in engine channel order.

name.description: Channel name as configured in the project, e.g. "Visibility", "WorldStatic", "Pawn". Pass it as `channel`.

object_type.description: An object type (WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, PhysicsBody, ...).

trace.description: Usable as a trace channel (Visibility, Camera, custom trace channels).

profiles.description: Collision profile names (BlockAll, OverlapAll, Pawn, Ragdoll, ...), sorted.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolCollisionChannels

tools.description:
Returns the simulation state, mass, velocity, collision and mobility of a body; for skeletal meshes also every bone body.
Returns: {component, simulating, gravity, collision_profile, collision, mobility, mass_kg, velocity, angular_velocity, bodies:[{bone, simulating, mass_kg}]}. Fails if the target has no primitive component.

target.description: Actor (its first primitive component, usually the root) or "actor#Component", e.g. "n12". (Reference to PrimitiveComponent: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path)

tools.name: physics.get_physics

returnValue.description: {component, simulating, gravity, collision_profile, collision, mobility, mass_kg, velocity, angular_velocity, bodies:[{bone, simulating, mass_kg}]}. Fails if the target has no primitive component.

bodies.description: Per-bone bodies of a skeletal mesh (empty for other components).

collision.description: Whether collision is enabled at all.

mass_kg.description: Mass in kg (0 without a physics body).

mobility.description: Static, Stationary or Movable. Only Movable components simulate.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolState

tools.description:
Traces a ray through the world and returns what it hits.
Returns: {hit, hits:[{actor, component, location, normal, distance}]} nearest first. Fails if neither end nor a non-zero direction is given, or the channel name is unknown (the channels are listed).

channel.description: Trace channel or object type name from get_collision_channels, e.g. "Visibility", "Camera", "WorldStatic", "Pawn".

complex.description: Trace per-triangle collision instead of simple shapes.

direction.description: Ray direction, e.g. [0,0,-1] (used when end is omitted). ([x, y, z] (cm))

distance.description: Ray length in cm when using direction.

end.description: Ray end [x,y,z]; or give direction (+ distance) instead. ([x, y, z] (cm))

ignore.description: Actors the ray passes through (node ids, paths, actor:Name).

items.description: Reference to Actor: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path

limit.description: Maximum hits with multi (0 = default list limit).

multi.description: Return every hit along the ray instead of the first blocking one.

start.description: Ray start [x,y,z] in cm, e.g. [0,0,500]. ([x, y, z] (cm))

tools.name: physics.line_trace

returnValue.description: {hit, hits:[{actor, component, location, normal, distance}]} nearest first. Fails if neither end nor a non-zero direction is given, or the channel name is unknown (the channels are listed).

hits.description: Hits nearest first (one entry unless multi).

actor.description: Reference of the hit actor (node id, else actor:Name).

distance.description: Distance from the start in cm.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolTraceResult

tools.description:
Finds actors overlapping a sphere or box.
Returns: {total, truncated, actors:[refs]} in query order. Fails if a box has no positive size, the radius is not positive, or the channel name is unknown.

center.description: Shape centre [x,y,z] in cm, e.g. [0,0,100]. ([x, y, z] (cm))

channel.description: Only bodies that overlap or block this channel (empty = every object type), e.g. "Pawn".

limit.description: Maximum actors returned (0 = default list limit).

size.description: Box size [x,y,z] in cm (shape Box). ([x, y, z] (cm))

tools.name: physics.overlap_test

returnValue.description: {total, truncated, actors:[refs]} in query order. Fails if a box has no positive size, the radius is not positive, or the channel name is unknown.

actors.description: References of the overlapping actors (node ids, else actor:Name).

truncated.description: True when actors were cut off by the limit.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolOverlapResult

tools.description:
Switches a skeletal mesh to ragdoll physics (or back). Undoable.
Returns: {target, ragdoll, bodies}. Fails if the actor has no skeletal mesh with a physics asset.

enabled.description: true for ragdoll, false to stop simulating the bodies.

target.description: Actor with a skeletal mesh that has a physics asset, e.g. "pawn". (Reference to Actor: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path)

tools.name: physics.ragdoll

returnValue.description: {target, ragdoll, bodies}. Fails if the actor has no skeletal mesh with a physics asset.

bodies.description: Physics bodies of the skeletal mesh.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolRagdollResult

tools.description:
Tunes how a body behaves: weight, grip, bounce, drag, gravity and axis locks. Only the settings you pass change. Works before or after set_simulate. Examples: a rolling barrel {friction:0.2, restitution:0.1, lock_translation:["y"]}; a bouncy ball {restitution:0.9}; a 2D game keeps bodies in the X/Z plane with lock_translation:["y"], lock_rotation:["x","z"].
Returns: The body state. Fails if the target has no collision or a lock axis is not x, y or z.

continuous_collision.description: CCD for fast objects that must not pass through thin walls.

lock_rotation.description: Axes it cannot rotate around, e.g. ["x","z"] (only spins around y).

lock_translation.description: World axes it cannot move along, e.g. ["y"].

target.description: Actor or "actor#Component", e.g. "n12". (Reference to PrimitiveComponent: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path)

tools.name: physics.set_body

returnValue.description: The body state. Fails if the target has no collision or a lock axis is not x, y or z.

bodies.description: Per-bone bodies of a skeletal mesh (empty for other components).

collision.description: Whether collision is enabled at all.

mass_kg.description: Mass in kg (0 without a physics body).

mobility.description: Static, Stationary or Movable. Only Movable components simulate.

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolState

tools.description:
Turns physics simulation on or off. A Static or Stationary component is switched to Movable first (reported in the result). Undoable: undo stops simulating and puts the object back where it was (re-attached).
Returns: {target, simulating, mobility_changed, note}. Fails if the component has no collision (physics cannot simulate without it).

enabled.description: true to simulate, false to stop.

target.description: Actor or "actor#Component", e.g. "n12". (Reference to PrimitiveComponent: node id (n12), node path, actor:Name or object path)

tools.name: physics.set_simulate

returnValue.description: {target, simulating, mobility_changed, note}. Fails if the component has no collision (physics cannot simulate without it).

mobility_changed.description: True when the component was Static/Stationary and was switched to Movable to simulate (undo restores it).

note.description: Extra information (e.g. what changed besides simulation).

returnValue.title: PhysicsToolSimulateResult
